keyVerseText: And when a convenient day was come, that Herod on his birthday made a supper to his lords, high captains, and chief estates of Galilee;
rootMeaning: The Greek adjective εὔκαιρος (eúkairos) derives from the combination of εὖ (eû), meaning "good" or "well," and καιρός (kairós), which refers to an appointed or opportune time. Together, εὔκαιρος conveys the sense of something that is well-timed or occurring at a favorable moment. This root meaning highlights not just a convenient time, but a divinely appointed or fitting season, emphasizing the qualitative goodness of the timing rather than simply chronological placement.
usageInScripture: The word εὔκαιρος appears twice in the New Testament, consistently conveying the idea of a well-timed or seasonable moment. Its translations such as "when a convenient" and "time of need" illustrate its use to describe moments that are especially suitable or opportune, often in relation to God's providential timing. This consistency underscores the importance of divine timing in Scripture, where events unfold not merely by chance but according to God’s perfect schedule.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding εὔκαιρος enriches our grasp of God’s sovereignty over time and circumstance. It reminds believers that God’s interventions and blessings come at the right moment, perfectly timed to meet our needs or fulfill His purposes. This word encourages trust in God’s providential care, assuring us that His timing is always "good" and "well-suited," even when it challenges our human expectations. Recognizing the significance of divine timing deepens faith and patience, as believers learn to wait for and walk in step with God’s appointed seasons.
keyVerseReflection: In Mark 6:21, the phrase "when a convenient day was come" uses εὔκαιρος to highlight the opportune timing of Herod’s birthday feast. This word draws attention to the moment as seasonable and fitting for the event, suggesting that the timing was not random but notable. The use of εὔκαιρος here helps the reader understand that certain moments carry a special significance, setting the stage for the unfolding narrative with a sense of divine or providential timing.
